text: Given a valid Umbrella API key/secret pair, When cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys is called, Then it returns the account's API key list (id, label, scope, status) and no key contains a secret field
Given a real Managed Provider Umbrella account, When cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys is called end to end, Then the live response is a non-empty array and no item contains a secret field
steps: Set UMBRELLA_API_KEY/UMBRELLA_KEY_SECRET to a real MSPbots test account (needs a real vendor account)
Call cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys via the local stdio server
expect: Non-empty array of key objects (id, label/keyType, scope, status); grep the raw response for any secret-like field and confirm none is present
notes: needs a real vendor account; not executed during design

text: Given organization_id=A, When cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists is called, Then the request is scoped via X-Umbrella-OrgId at token-mint time, matching the existing reports.py pattern

Given two different managed customers (org A, org B) on a real Managed Provider account, When cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists is called once per org, Then the two responses are disjoint (no cross-tenant data)
steps: Resolve two organization_id values via cisco_umbrella_list_customers (needs a real vendor account with 2+ managed customers)
Call cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists with org A's id
Call cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists with org B's id
expect: The two destination-list responses are disjoint (different ids/names), proving org A's call never leaks org B's policy data and vice versa
notes: needs a real vendor account with at least 2 managed customers; mirrors the existing org-scope test already in this repo

text: Given organization_id=A, When cisco_umbrella_list_application_lists and cisco_umbrella_get_application_usage are called, Then both return that customer's application-list/usage data via GET /policies/v2/applicationLists and GET /policies/v2/applications/usage
Given any domain name, When cisco_umbrella_get_domain_categorization is called, Then it returns Cisco's security/content categorization for that domain without requiring organization_id

Given any domain name, When cisco_umbrella_get_domain_risk_score and cisco_umbrella_get_domain_whois are called, Then each returns the expected shape (numeric risk score; WHOIS record with registrant/registrar/nameServers)

Given a gateway-mode request missing the X-Umbrella-Api-Key/X-Umbrella-Key-Secret headers, When any of the 8 new tools is called, Then it returns the same not_configured structured error the existing 14 tools return

Given an upstream 401/403/404/429/5xx response from any new endpoint, When the corresponding tool is called, Then it returns the same structured error_envelope with the same status-to-code mapping as the existing tools (no stack trace, no raw HTML)
